mood.summary: Fear is still running high. On Nov 5 the S&P 500 fell 4.4% and the Nasdaq slid into a correction, the worst day since April 2025, on worries that election results will slow AI and data-centre spending. The Fear & Greed index sits in Extreme Fear at 20, and bearish individual investors outnumber bulls by about 14 points. Stocks are bouncing on Nov 6 after a strong jobs report (165,000 jobs vs about 60,000 expected), but that also firmed bets on a December Fed rate hike.

trending.note: Board as of Thursday 4:08 PM ET; prices are the 2026-11-12 close. Why-it's-trending notes summarize the Stocktwits stream and the news it links to.

items.name: NVIDIA Corp
items.about: Designs the GPUs and networking systems that power most AI data centers.
items.why: Jensen Huang resigned as CEO on Nov 12 after reports of a second workplace relationship, and CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO. The stock fell as much as 14% at the open but recovered to close down about 4.3% at $166.20; earnings are due Nov 17.

items.name: Tesla Inc
items.about: Makes electric vehicles, batteries and energy storage, and is building self-driving and robot businesses.
items.why: Bloomberg reported on Nov 12 that SpaceX and Tesla merger talks are progressing and a deal could be announced as early as December, though no terms are agreed. Shares rose 1.7% to about $397.48; posts debate what premium Tesla holders might get.

items.name: Cardinal Infrastructure Group Inc
items.about: Builds civil infrastructure such as roads, utilities and site development projects in the US Southeast.
items.why: Shares fell about 62% to $5.66 after a Q3 loss of $0.21 a share versus expected profit, an adjusted EBITDA margin that fell to 4.2% from 17.5%, and withdrawn 2026 guidance. The company also delayed its Hughes Brothers deal and approved a $50M buyback; William Blair downgraded the stock.

items.name: Novavax Inc
items.about: Develops protein-based vaccines, including its COVID-19 shot, partnered with Sanofi.
items.why: Shares fell about 12% to $8.76, extending a slide after recent Q3 results that included a $125M Sanofi milestone. No new company news was found for the day; posts vent about the partnership strategy and some link the drop to wider market weakness.

items.name: Nebius Group N.V.
items.about: Runs AI cloud data centers that rent out Nvidia GPU capacity.
items.why: Nebius beat Q3 revenue estimates but said 2026 revenue will land at the low end of its range because new data-center capacity is coming online later, and guided 2027 capex to $40B–$45B. Shares fell about 17% to $128.91, also caught in the AI-infrastructure selloff after Nvidia's CEO exit.

items.name: Applied Materials Inc.
items.about: Sells the machines chipmakers use to deposit, etch and inspect semiconductor wafers.
items.why: Applied Materials reported after the close: record quarterly revenue of $10.41B, up 53% from a year ago, and non-GAAP EPS of $4.16, above its own guidance. Shares closed down 3.5% at $381.21 before the report and were little changed after hours.

items.name: Cisco Systems, Inc.
items.about: Sells networking gear, security and collaboration software to businesses and cloud providers.
items.why: Cisco reported fiscal Q1 revenue of $18.5B, up 24% and above its $18.0B–$18.2B guidance, and raised its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to $74.8B–$75.8B. The stock closed up 1.1% at $101.90 and jumped about 5–8% after hours.

items.name: Cerebras Systems Inc
items.about: Designs wafer-scale AI chips and systems used for training and running large AI models.
items.why: Cerebras reported Q3 results after the close, against a consensus of about $215M in revenue and a 14-cent loss. Shares closed down 3.2% at $97.83 and swung sharply after hours; posts show traders split on the numbers.

items.name: Intuitive Machines Inc
items.about: Builds lunar landers and space data and navigation services, largely for NASA.
items.why: Intuitive Machines posted record Q3 revenue of $269.3M, above estimates of about $246M, with a $1.9B backlog and 2026 revenue guidance of $920M–$950M. Shares gained 7% to $13.04 after being up as much as 20% intraday.

items.name: Flowers Foods, Inc.
items.about: Bakes packaged bread and snack cakes sold under brands like Nature's Own and Dave's Killer Bread.
items.why: Flowers Foods reported Q3 results after the close; analysts expected EPS of $0.15, down about 35% from a year ago. Shares slipped 3.9% to $6.01 in regular trading and fell further after hours; posts focus on the cut dividend and weak bread demand.

items.name: Super Micro Computer Inc
items.about: Builds servers and storage systems, including Nvidia GPU servers for AI data centers.
items.why: Shares fell about 11% to $26.99 as Nvidia's leadership crisis revived questions about chip-smuggling cases involving Singapore-based Megaspeed. Posts say Supermicro's CFO denied dealings with Megaspeed; that claim could not be confirmed.

items.name: Zoom Communications Inc.
items.about: Provides video meetings, phone and contact-center software for businesses.
items.why: Zoom ended about flat at $97.73 after an afternoon dip. Posts link the move to Anthropic's launch of Claude Meetings, an AI meeting product, while others note Zoom's stake in Anthropic; the launch was not independently confirmed in news searches.

items.name: Nu Holdings Ltd
items.about: Runs Nubank, a digital bank serving customers in Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
items.why: Nu reported Q3 results after the close, with consensus around $0.23 EPS and $5.96B in revenue. Shares fell 4.3% to $11.79 in regular trading; posts say the results beat expectations.

items.name: Microsoft Corp
items.about: Sells Windows, Office 365, Azure cloud services and AI tools such as Copilot.
items.why: Microsoft rose 0.4% to $522.99 while posts focused on an Outlook outage late in the session. The cause and scope of the outage were not confirmed in news searches.

items.name: Advanced Micro Devices Inc
items.about: Designs CPUs and AI accelerators for PCs, servers and data centers.
items.why: AMD rose about 5.9% to $585.63 as investors rotated into Nvidia rivals after Jensen Huang's resignation; Broadcom also gained. The rally helped the Nasdaq 100 recover from its early losses.

items.name: Direxion Daily TSLA Bull 2X Shares
items.about: Exchange-traded fund that aims for twice Tesla's daily stock move.
items.why: The 2x Tesla fund rose 3.4% to $10.77 as Tesla gained on reports that SpaceX merger talks are progressing. Because it resets daily, it moves about twice as much as Tesla each day.

items.name: CRISPR Therapeutics AG
items.about: Develops CRISPR gene-editing therapies, including Casgevy for sickle cell disease.
items.why: Shares fell 6.8% to $42.63 with no company news found for the day. Posts note the stock broke a level that had held for about 18 months and debate recent trial data from CRISPR and Intellia.

items.name: AGNC Investment Corp
items.about: Real estate investment trust that holds US government-backed mortgage bonds and pays a monthly dividend.
items.why: AGNC fell 3.4% to $8.20 as the 10-year Treasury yield returned to about 5% and traders weighed the chance of a December Fed hike. Posts note heavy put buying in the options market.

items.name: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd
items.about: Runs China's largest e-commerce marketplaces plus a major cloud and AI business.
items.why: Alibaba fell about 7% to $94.34 after The Information reported the US is preparing rules to stop Chinese AI firms from renting advanced chips in overseas data centers. Nvidia's turmoil and Alibaba's reported ties to Megaspeed added pressure; results are due Nov 19.

items.name: ImmunityBio Inc
items.about: Develops immunotherapies; its main product, Anktiva, treats a form of bladder cancer.
items.why: Shares fell 9.1% to $6.07, extending a drop since Q3 results on Nov 9 that missed forecasts and included a going-concern warning. Posts focus on dilution risk and the lack of new revenue sources.
